- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast above 1–2% of recent high.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.00 to 1.00), model reacts too quickly; delay peak forecast by 1–3 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend after a spike, check for mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 1–3% above model, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for next forecast if sentiment remains stable.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.50–0.67 range, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and model forecasts high, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
